claims.statement: Meta documents a Page Access Token, obtained by exchanging a user access token, that lets an app read, write and modify data belonging to a Facebook Page.

sources.supports: Page access tokens let you read, write, and modify data belonging to a Facebook Page. To obtain one, first get a user access token, then exchange it for a Page access token via the Graph API.
sources.locator: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies, Page Access Tokens

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Only existence is established. The access-tokens page states that token length changes over time and gives no format grammar; it is not recorded here.
Whether a Page token is distinguishable from a user token by form is not stated; examples in the pages read are truncated placeholders and are not a format statement.

Leads, not claims: one scanner rule artifact (Gitleaks, pinned in source github-com-gitleaks-gitleaks-d47395c7b2) treats strings starting with the literal prefixes EAAM or EAAC followed by 100 or more alphanumeric characters as a Facebook Page access token candidate, and another (Nosey Parker, source github-com-praetorian-inc-noseyparker-8d6f62ccdb) treats a longer literal older prefix as a generic Facebook access token. They name different token kinds, so no corroborated claim is made and no family attribution is drawn. A Meta page stating a token grammar would settle it.
